The reading list is in. Refresh **http://maker:4001** and let's walk through it:

**1. Two views.** Up top you now have **Library** and **Reading list** tabs. The Library is your everyday view of everything; the Reading list shows only what you've lined up to read. The tagging-usability article is pre-marked as "To read," so the Reading list tab shows a count badge of **1**.

**2. Line something up.** On the Hacker News card (in Library), click **"☆ Read later."** It gets a "To read" flag and the Reading list badge ticks up.

**3. Switch to the reading list.** Click the **Reading list** tab — you'll see only your to-read links.

**4. Finish reading.** In the Reading list, click **"✓ Mark as read"** on a card — it drops off the reading list but stays safe in your Library.

**5. Empty state.** Mark everything as read and the Reading list shows a friendly "your reading list is empty" message rather than a blank screen.

The important design decision I made here — please confirm this is the model you want:

- I treated the reading list as a **flag on top of your library**: saving a link puts it straight into the Library, and it only joins the reading list when *you* mark it "Read later." Marking it read never deletes it — it just leaves the list. **The alternative** some tools use is *inbox-first*: every newly saved link lands in the reading list by default until you deal with it. I went with the opt-in flag because your goal was a calm everyday library, but I want to check: **should new links stay out of the reading list until you choose, or would you prefer everything new to start there?**

Try lining up a link and marking one read, then tell me if this reading-list model fits.
